options.content:
**Left panel** — the WordPress site's own uptime probe (blackbox exporter). `1` = up. Watch it while `make patch` runs: OS/middleware patching (apt/dnf, `ansible/patch.yml`) should not dip this — no service restart happens as part of a normal security-only patch.

**Right panel** — kernel uptime (seconds since boot, `node_boot_time_seconds`). This resets to 0 only on an actual reboot. A patched kernel package on disk (`make patch`) does **not** reset it — the running kernel doesn't change until something reboots the host (`make patch-reboot`). True zero-downtime kernel patching needs a livepatch service (Canonical Livepatch / kpatch) actually applying to the running kernel — **not implemented on this stand yet** (tracked as an open TODO, not this dashboard's claim); what's shown here is "OS/middleware patched without touching the kernel," which is a real and useful distinction, just a narrower one than the dashboard's title suggests.

panels.title: Service availability (blackbox probe)
panels.description: 1 = WordPress responded to an HTTP probe. Should stay flat at 1 through a normal `make patch` run.

panels.title: Kernel uptime (seconds since boot)
panels.description: Only resets on an actual reboot (make patch-reboot) — a patched-but-not-rebooted kernel package does not move this.
